title: Senior Learning Designer Training Plan (TP) and Master Lesson Plans (MLPs)
description: This requirement is for the Department of National Defence (DND) The Canadian Armed Forces (CAF) requires the provision of a Learning Advisor for RCEME School Qualification Standard (QS) for EO TECH RQ-PTE. The Contractor must create a 165-day (33 weeks) or less technical TP and MLP that aligns with the five Performance Objectives of the EO TECH RQ-PTE QS, which will be provided in Appendix Electronic-Optics Technician Qualification Standard as the primary reference for curriculum alignment. The Crown retains the rights to negotiate with suppliers on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada

title: Training Facility for Vehicle Technician Training
description: Request for information Background: The Canadian Army needs to train members. Traditionally this was done using military facilities, support structures and DND staff. It is no longer possible to keep all training completely in-house. There is a need to approach external training institutions and organizations to help fill this gap. Objectives: This request is issued to understand what is available and to learn what is possible or not possible to help us develop our training requirements as well as work towards potential future contracts. This is not a bid solicitation or request for offers and this request will not result in the award of any contract at this time. Questions to Industry - Respondents are requested to provide answers to the questions listed in the RFI, if possible. Respondents may also respond with suggestions or alternatives. Respondents with questions regarding this document may direct their enquiries to the Contracting Authority via email: procurementCADTC@forces.gc.ca Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada.

title: Portable Digital Radiography Kits
description: NOTICE OF PROPOSED PROCUREMENT The Department of National Defence (DND) requires the purchase of Portable Digital Radiography Kits, in order to meet its inspection requirements. The resulting Contract will contain initial and optional deliverables which may be purchased for a period until 31 March 2030. Delivery of the items is within Ottawa, Ontario Initial Deliverables: Must be received on or before 31 March 2027 Initial Deliverables Description: Portable Digital Radiography Kits.-- Quantity:(6) Optional Deliverables Optional Deliverables 1 April 2027 to 31 March 2028 Description: Portable Digital Radiography Kits.-- Quantity:(2) Optional Deliverables 1 April 2028 to 31 March 2029 Description: Portable Digital Radiography Kits.-- Quantity:(2) Optional Deliverables 1 April 2029 to 31 March 2030 Description: Portable Digital Radiography Kits.-- Quantity:(2) Tendering procedures: This solicitation of offers is subject to the Policy on Reciprocal Procurement. This means that only Canadian Suppliers and Suppliers of an Applicable Trading Partner, as defined in the Annex Solicitation of Offers Definitions, are eligible for this solicitation of offers. Offers submitted by Suppliers of a Non-Trading Partner will be rejected. Nature of Requirement: The Department of National Defence (DND), is responsible for the security and safety of Defence installations, buildings and facilities, including the detection of concealed threats. In order to facilitate these activities, DND requires the purchase of Portable Digital Radiography Kits, capable of locating and identifying threats. Detailed requirements may be found within the attached Solicitation of Offers and any amendments to the Solicitation of Offers. Delivery Date (initial deliverables): On or before 31 March 2027. Competitive Procurement Strategy: For Canada to declare an offer compliant, the offer must comply with the requirements of the solicitation of offers and meet all mandatory technical evaluation criteria. Canada will consider the compliant offer with the lowest evaluated price for award. Security Requirements: There is no security requirement associated with this Solicitation of Offers. File Number: W8474-278722 The Crown retains the rights to negotiate with suppliers on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada

title: Notice of Proposed Procurement (NPP) - Data Hub Invitation to Qualify (ITQ) - D
description: Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC) is providing advance notice of its intention to issue a new Invitation to Qualify (ITQ-D) in support of the Enterprise Data Hub initiative. PSPC has previously conducted procurement and industry engagement activities related to the Enterprise Data Hub, including previous Invitations to Qualify. PSPC now intends to launch a new ITQ-D through CanadaBuys. This Notice of Proposed Procurement (NPP) is being published for information purposes only to provide interested suppliers with advance awareness of the forthcoming procurement opportunity. No solicitation documents are being released through this notice, and suppliers are not required to respond at this time. The forthcoming ITQ-D will set out the applicable requirements, qualification process, evaluation criteria, and instructions for participation. Interested suppliers are encouraged to monitor CanadaBuys for the release of the ITQ-D and any related procurement notices. For additional background on the Enterprise Data Hub initiative and industry engagement activities conducted to date, interested suppliers may also review the previously published Summary of Feedback and Outcomes Report.

title: Canadian Student Alcohol and Drugs Survey (CSADS).
description: Please note that late submissions will not be considered or accepted. All required supporting documentation and bid submission must be submitted by October 29, 2026 at 2:00pm EST. All bids submitted after 2:00pm EST will result in the bid being declared non-responsive. Description Canada is seeking proposals for professional survey research and project management services to plan, coordinate, administer, and deliver the Canadian Student Alcohol and Drugs Survey (CSADS). The survey will gather nationally and provincially representative data from at least 36,000 students in Grades 7 to 12 across Canada to support Health Canada’s surveillance activities and evidence-based policies and programs related to youth substance use. The requirement is subject to security requirements and includes the possibility of two additional three-year option periods. description: Sähkökäyttöiset nivellinja-autot ja niiden huolenpitosopimus Plusbussi-liikenteeseen Tampereen Kaupunkiliikenne Oy pyytää avoimeen hankintamenettelyyn perustuen tarjouksia kahdestakymmenestäkahdesta (22) uudesta sähkökäyttöisestä nivellinja-autosta tämän tarjouspyynnön ja sen liitteiden mukaisesti, sisältäen myös tarjoushinnan autojen huolenpitosopimuksesta sopimusajaksi (optiopalvelu 10+5 vuotta) tämän tarjouspyynnön ja sen liitteiden mukaisesti. Liikennöinti ajoneuvoilla käynnistyy 7.8.2028 alkaen tai liikenteen tilaajan ilmoittaman myöhemmän ajankohdan mukaisesti. Yksi auto toimitetaan hankintayksikölle koulutuskäyttöön 1.5.2028 mennessä. Muut autot (ei koske 10 lisäauton optiota) toimitetaan hankintayksikölle elokuun 2028 alusta lukien liikennöinnin käynnistymisen mukaisesti.,

description: Hankinnan kohteena on ratkaisu, jonka avulla voidaan tarjota tietoturvallisesti eristetty ja hallittu palvelinsäilö varmuuskopioidulle datalle. Ratkaisun tulee mahdollistaa varmuuskopioiden turvallinen säilytys, käsittely ja hyödyntäminen erillisessä, tuotantoympäristöstä irrotetussa kokonaisuudessa. TIETOJENKÄSITTELYN OIKEUTUS, SIJAINTI, HALLINTAYHTEYDET JA SUOJAUS Hankinnan kohteena oleva palvelimen turvasäilö -palvelu sisältää Tilaajan varmistusympäristöstä replikoitavaa varmistusdataa, joka voi sisältää Tilaajan oman datan ohella myös mm. omistaja-asiakkaiden potilastietojärjestelmien tietoja ja siten EU:n yleisen tietosuoja-asetuksen 9 artiklassa tarkoitettuja erityisiin henkilötietoryhmiin kuuluvia henkilötietoja. Erityisiin henkilötietoryhmiin kuuluvien tietojen käsittely on lähtökohtaisesti kiellettyä, mutta käsittely on sallittua, kun kieltoon on säädetty poikkeus. Tässä palvelussa käsittely on välttämätöntä terveydenhuollon tietojärjestelmien ja palvelujen hallinnoimiseksi sekä palvelujen jatkuvuuden ja palautettavuuden varmistamiseksi (GDPR 9(2)(h)). Käsittely toteutetaan omistaja-asiakkaiden (rekisterinpitäjien) ohjeiden mukaisesti; Tilaaja toimii henkilötietojen käsittelijänä ja vastaa alikäsittelijöiden (Toimittaja mahdollisine alihankkijoineen) hallinnasta. Rekisterinpitäjien osoitusvelvollisuuden, valvottavuuden ja käsiteltävien tietojen korkean suojaustason varmistamiseksi Tilaaja edellyttää, että: 1) varmistusdata säilytetään ja sitä käsitellään yksinomaan Suomen alueella sijaitsevissa konesaleissa, ja 2) myös palvelun hallintayhteydet (ylläpito- ja hallintaliikenne sekä mahdolliset etähallintaratkaisut) ovat sallittuja vain Suomen alueelta, ja 3) varmistusdata on salattuna (siirrossa ja levossa) ja palvelu tuotetaan ainoastaan Tilaajalle dedikoidussa ympäristössä. Vaatimus on rajattu koskemaan vain hankinnan kohteena olevaa varmistuspalvelua ja on oikeassa suhteessa hankinnan tavoitteeseen ja käsiteltävien tietojen luonteeseen nähden. OPTIO Optiona pyydetään hinnoittelua analytiikkapalvelulle (Eristetty analytiikkaympäristö ransomware- ja virusskannauksineen), joka toimii täysin erillisessä verkkovyöhykkeessä ilman pääsyä tuotantoverkkoon. Kyseistä palvelua voidaan hankkia sopimusaikana tarpeen mukaan, minkä vuoksi se on vertailuhinnassa mukana vain yhden vuoden osalta.

title: Finland – Construction work – Tupurin koulun ja päiväkodin peruskorjauksen hankinta
description: Salon kaupunki (jäljempänä hankintayksikkö / tilaaja) pyytää tarjouksia Tupurin koulun ja päiväkodin peruskorjauksen hankinnasta kokonaisurakkana tämän tarjouspyynnön ja sen liitteenä olevien urakka-asiakirjojen ja suunnitelmien mukaisesti. Hankinnan kohteena on osoitteessa Taimistokatu 1 sijaitseva peruskorjattava Tupurin koulu ja päiväkoti. Urakkamuotona on kokonaisurakka. Urakkasuoritukseen sisältyvät kaikki kohteen suunnitelma-asiakirjoissa esitetyt työt, materiaalit, hankinnat ja velvoitteet, ellei suunnitelmissa muuta mainita. Urakoitsijan tulee huomioida tarjouksessaan, että urakka toteutetaan kolmevaiheisena ja urakan aikana koulu ja päiväkoti toimivat rakennuksessa ja pihapiirissä. Urakoitsijan tulee huomioida urakan luonteesta johtuvasta yhteensovittamisesta, sekä vaiheistamisesta ja koulun toiminnan turvaamisesta urakkaan aiheutuvat kustannukset. Tilaaja katsoo lisä- ja muutostyöksi vain lopullisen toteutuksen suunnitelmamuutokset. Kaikista väliaikaisista ratkaisuista ja niiden aiheuttamista kustannuksista vastaa urakoitsija. Kokonaisurakkamuoto on valittu hankkeen laajuuden, pitkän toteutusajan ja kokonaisuuden hallittavuuden vuoksi. Urakkamuoto tukee hankkeen tehokasta johtamista sekä aikataulun, kustannusten ja laadun hallintaa. Hankkeen toteutuksen merkittävin erityispiirre on se, että koulu ja päiväkoti ovat käytössä koko rakennushankkeen ajan väistötilaratkaisujen tukemana. Työturvallisuus, työmaan logistiikka, käyttäjäturvallisuus sekä häiriötön opetuksen ja varhaiskasvatuksen toiminta ovat hankkeen keskeisiä onnistumistekijöitä. Urakan tulee olla valmis vaiheittain seuraavasti. Rakennustöiden tulee olla vaiheittain valmiit ja vastaanotettu (sisätilat), sekä rakennusvalvonnan käyttöönottokatselmus vaiheen osalta suoritettu: • Rakennustyöt vaihe 1. (päiväkoti) 22.12.2027 • Rakennustyöt vaihe 2. (koulu, vanha osa) 22.12.2028 • Rakennustyöt vaihe 3. (koulu uusi osa) 1.8.2029 • Koulun keittiön saneeraustyöt tulee tehdä 1.6-15.8 2028 välisenä aikana. Välitavoitteet pihatöiden osalta: • Saattoliikennealue ja päiväkodin leikkipiha valmis ja vastaanotettu 31.7.2027 Kokonaisurakka julkisivu- vesikatto- ja pihatöineen valmis ja vastaanotettu 3.12.2029. Urakan aikataulu voi muuttua tarjouspyynnössä kuvatulla tavalla.

description: 1. Hankinnan kohde Hankinnan kohteena on aloittavien yritysten neuvonta- ja valmennuspalvelukokonaisuus, joka muodostuu kahdesta toisiaan täydentävästä osa-alueesta: 1. yrityksen perustamisneuvonnasta yritystoimintaa suunnitteleville henkilöille sekä 2. yrityksen käynnistämisvaiheen tuesta ja valmennuksesta vastaperustetuille yrityksille. Palvelujen tavoitteena on madaltaa yrittäjäksi ryhtymisen kynnystä, parantaa yritysten toimintaedellytyksiä sekä vahvistaa uusien yritysten elinkelpoisuutta ja jatkuvuutta ensimmäisten toimintavuosien aikana. Palvelukokonaisuuden tulee muodostaa yhtenäinen asiakaspolku liikeidean arvioinnista yrityksen alkuvaiheen kehittämiseen. Tällöin palveluntuottaja pystyy parhaalla mahdollisella tavalla tukemaan yritystoimintaa suunnittelevia henkilöitä yrityksen perustamisessa ja vahvistamaan yritysten elinkelpoisuutta ja kasvuedellytyksiä toiminnan alkuvaiheessa. Hankinnan ennakoitu kokonaisarvo optiokausi mukaan lukien on noin 780 000 euroa (alv 0 %). Tilaaja ei sitoudu tiettyihin hankintamääriin. 3. Käynnistämisvaiheen tukea tarjotaan Jyväskylään perustetuille tai pääasiallisesti Jyväskylässä toimiville yrityksille enintään 18 kuukauden ajan yrityksen perustamisesta. 4. Palvelun sisältö 4.1 Yrityksen perustamisneuvonta Palveluntuottajan tulee tarjota yritystoiminnan aloittamista suunnitteleville asiakkaille asiantuntevaa, maksutonta ja puolueetonta neuvontaa. Perustamisneuvonnan tulee sisältää vähintään: • henkilökohtainen yritysneuvonta • ryhmämuotoiset info- ja neuvontatilaisuudet • liikeidean arviointi • yrittäjävalmiuksien arviointi • liiketoimintasuunnitelman laadinnan ohjaus • talous- ja kannattavuuslaskelmien ohjaus • markkina- ja kilpailutilanteen arviointi • yritysmuodon valintaan liittyvä neuvonta • rahoitus-, lupa- ja viranomaisprosesseihin liittyvä ohjaus • yrityksen perustamiseen liittyvä käytännön ohjaus. Palveluntuottajan tulee kyetä palvelemaan asiakkaita suomeksi ja englanniksi. Muiden kielten osalta palveluntuottajan tulee kuvata käytettävät ratkaisut. 4.2 Yrityksen käynnistämisvaiheen tuki ja valmennus Palveluntuottajan tulee tarjota vastaperustetuille yrityksille suunnitelmallista tukea ja valmennusta yrityksen ensimmäisten toimintakuukausien aikana. Tuen tulee perustua mahdollisuuksien mukaan yrityksen perustamisvaiheessa laadittuihin suunnitelmiin, laskelmiin ja kehittämistoimenpiteisiin. Palveluntuottajan tulee varmistaa asiakkuuden saumaton jatkuminen perustamisvaiheesta käynnistämisvaiheen palveluihin. Käynnistämisvaiheen palvelun tulee sisältää vähintään: • yritystoiminnan alkuvaiheen tilannekartoitus • liiketoimintasuunnitelman päivittäminen • myynnin ja markkinoinnin kehittäminen • hinnoittelun ja kannattavuuden seuranta • talouden hallinnan ohjaus • kassavirran hallinnan tuki • digitaalisten työkalujen hyödyntämisen ohjaus • verkostojen ja yhteistyökumppaneiden tunnistaminen • kasvun ja kehittämisen mahdollisuuksien arviointi • yksilöllinen yritysvalmennus. Palvelun tulee olla asiakkaan käytettävissä enintään 18 kuukauden ajan yrityksen perustamisesta. 5. Palvelua tulee olla saatavilla: • lähitapaamisina • etäpalveluina • puhelin- ja verkkoneuvontana • ryhmätilaisuuksina. Palveluntuottajan tulee huolehtia asiakkaiden yhdenvertaisesta kohtelusta ja palvelujen saavutettavuudesta. 7. Tarjoajan soveltuvuus Tarjoajalla tulee olla: • riittävä kokemus aloittavien yritysten neuvonnasta tai yritysten kehittämispalveluiden tuottamisesta • käytettävissään riittävä määrä yritysneuvonnan asiantuntijoita • osaaminen yrityksen perustamisesta, liiketoiminnan suunnittelusta, yritysrahoituksesta, taloudesta ja yritysten kehittämisestä • valmius tuottaa palvelua monikanavaisesti • asiakasohjausmalli yrittäjän osaamisen vahvistamiseksi Jyväskylän seudun koulutustarjontaa hyödyntäen • dokumentoitu laadunhallintamalli ja vähintään kahden vuoden kokemus ao. laadunhallintamallin toteuttamisesta Tarjoajan soveltuvuutta arvioidaan soveltuvuusvaatimusten ja laatukriteerien perusteella.

title: 6515--Digital Non-Mydriatic Retinal Camera
description: Digital Non-Mydriatic Fundus Camera System This announcement requests information from industry to support market research and preliminary acquisition planning for the procurement of (1) one digital non-mydriatic fundus camera system with retinal image-capture software and vendor installation for the new East Indianapolis VA Clinic Tele-Eye Screening room. Of particular interest is identifying products that are made in America and meet the domestic end-product test of FAR 25.101. This is not a solicitation for proposals. No contract will be awarded from this notice. REQUIREMENT The agency is seeking information on sources of supply for one digital non-mydriatic fundus camera system with retinal image-capture software. Description: Compact, non-mydriatic digital retinal imaging system designed to acquire high-resolution color and fundus autofluorescence images of the human retina. The system shall support screening, documentation, and monitoring of ocular conditions without routinely requiring pharmacological pupil dilation. Salient Characteristics: Shall provide color retinal photography and fundus autofluorescence imaging. Shall produce retinal images with a resolution of at least 32 megapixels. Shall use infrared light for patient alignment and focusing before image capture. Shall acquire images through pupils approximately 3.3 mm in diameter or smaller without routinely requiring dilation. Shall provide automated alignment, focusing, exposure adjustment, image capture, and switching between anterior-eye and retinal observation. Shall permit the operator to override automatic focusing and manually adjust focus when necessary. Shall automatically evaluate image focus and eye alignment and alert the operator when image quality is insufficient. Shall provide digital image-processing modes capable of emphasizing retinal vascular and structural features, including red-free and blue-spectrum viewing modes. Shall include contrast-enhancement processing to improve differentiation between retinal blood vessels and surrounding tissue. Shall use low-intensity flash illumination to minimize pupil constriction and support sequential image acquisition. Shall provide adjustable image-sensitivity settings covering a range equivalent to ISO 200 through ISO 6400. Shall include an integrated display that allows the operator to preview and verify captured images at the imaging device. Shall include a complete retinal image-capture and management software package supporting image acquisition, patient-data entry or import, image review, processing, storage, and export of retinal images and associated patient information in DICOM and commonly used image formats. The software shall support DICOM worklist and electronic medical record integration when properly configured. Minimum of one-year manufacturer warranty coverage. Interested parties who can provide a product that meets the description above are requested to submit the following information: Product information documenting salient characteristics, Company name, address and point of contact with phone number, SAM Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), Place of manufacture, Socio-economic status to identify the business class as a large business, SDVOSB, VOSB, small business, Woman Owned, etc., Any other pertinent company documentation. Note: All interested parties must be registered in SAM (System for Award Management) to be eligible for the award of a future Government contract. Send submissions to Brian.Rosciszewski@VA.gov., reference 36C25027Q0097 in email subject. This market research is for informational and planning purposes. This is not a solicitation and does not obligate the Government to issue a solicitation. Please be advised that the government will not pay any costs for responses and information submitted. Respondents may not be notified of the results of this notice; it is at the discretion of the Government to release any results. Thanks in advance for your time and consideration in supporting America s veterans. ** End of Sources Sought Notice **

title: Pk-yritysbarometrin toteuttaminen vuodelle 2027 (VN/20171/2026)
description: Pk-yritysbarometrin toteuttaminen vuodelle 2027 (VN/20171/2026) Tarjouspyynnön kohde Hankinnan kohteena on pk-yritysten suhdanneodotuksia selvittävän barometrin tiedonkeruun ja raportoinnin toteuttaminen kahdesti vuodessa. Pk-yritysbarometrissa kuvataan pienten ja keski-suurten yritysten toimintaa ja niiden taloudellista toimintaympäristöä. Tarkastelun kohteena ovat pk-yritysten suhdanneodotukset ja niiden kehitys, kasvu ja uudistuminen. Lisäksi käsitellään kansainvälistymistä, investointeja ja rahoitusta. Ensimmäinen barometrin kyselykierros toteutetaan joulu- tammikuussa (julkistaminen helmikuun puolivälissä) ja toinen heinä- elokuussa (julkistaminen syyskuun puoliväliin mennessä) vuonna 2027. Ensimmäinen kysely käynnistyisi siis joulukuussa 2026 ja kyselylomakkeen päivittäminen marraskuussa 2026. Esimerkit kysymyslomakkeesta ovat liitteinä. Kysymyslomakkeen pituus on enintään 50 kysymystä. Kullekin kierrokselle kysymyslomake vahvistetaan kuitenkin aina erikseen. Osa kysymyksistä on vaihtuvia. Lisäksi joitain aihepiirejä tarkastellaan sekä suppealla että laajalla kysymyspatteristolla siten, että osa kysymyksistä sisältyy vain kevään tai syksyn barometriin. Kysely tehdään suomeksi ja ruotsiksi. Lomakkeen käännöstyöstä vastaa tilaaja. Kohdejoukko ja otos Kyselyn kohdejoukkona ovat pk-yritykset (alle 250 henkilöä työllistävät). Otosjoukko muodostetaan siten, että se rakenteeltaan (alueellisuus, toimialajako ja henkilökunnan koko) vastaa mahdollisimman hyvin pk-yritysrakennetta Suomessa. Otantakehikkona on käytetty TOL 2008 toimiala-luokitusta ja Tilastokeskuksen Yritysrekisteriä tai muuta laajapohjaista yritystietokantaa. Toimittajalla tulee olla käytössään yritysten yhteystietojen hankintaan soveltuva kattava rekisteri, jota voidaan tarvittaessa täydentää Suomen Yrittäjien jäsenrekisterin tiedoin. Toimittajan tulee seurata vastaajajoukkoa ja siihen perustuvien tulosten edustavuutta tiedonkeruiden aikana. Toimittajan tulee poimia otokseen ja saada vastaukset riittävältä määrältä yrityksiä siten, että alueellinen, toimialoittainen ja henkilökunnan kokoluokittainen edustavuus toteutuu. Yleensä pk-yritysbarometrin tietopohjana on ollut noin 4 500–6 000 vastanneen yrityksen tiedot. Kysely toteutetaan pääasiassa internetkyselynä, jota voidaan täydentää mobiilipohjaisella kyselyllä. title: Mechanical Maintenance Services – RCMP Arviat and Cambridge Bay, NU
description: Description: The Royal Canadian Mounted Police in Arviat and Cambridge Bay, Nunavut Territories, has a requirement for the Supply and Delivery of Mechanical Maintenance Services at the RCMP Arviat Detachment and Cambridge Bay Detachment. This procurement is subject to the Nunavut Land Claims Agreement and the Directive on Government Contracts, Including Real Property Leases, in the Nunavut Settlement Area. Bidders are requested to maximize Inuit employment, subcontracting and on-the-job training opportunities, and involve Inuit businesses, in carrying out the work under this project. The Nunavut Agreement contains a provision requiring the inclusion of socio-economic bid criteria in the solicitation document, when practicable and consistent with sound procurement management principles. These socio-economic bid criteria are referred to as Nunavut Benefits Criteria (NBC) and Inuit Benefits Criteria (IBC), and bidders propose Inuit benefits in their bid submission via an Inuit Benefits Plan (IBP). Policy on Reciprocal Procurement This solicitation of bids is open only to Canadian suppliers and to Suppliers of an applicable trading partner. Delivery Date: The contract period will be for 12-months from the date of contract. Security: This requirement contains a security requirement. Basis of selection: A bid must comply with all the requirements of the bid solicitation and meet all mandatory requirements. Bids not meeting the requirements will be declared non-responsive. The selection will be based on the highest responsive combined rating of total Inuit Benefits Plan (IBP) merit, technical merit and price. The ratio will be 30% for the total IBP merit, 30 % for the technical merit and 40% for price. Tenders must be submitted to the RCMP Bid Receiving Unit at: NWR_Procurement_Bids@rcmp-grc.gc.ca Refer to the attached tender documents to obtain further information. Canada retains the right to negotiate with any supplier on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada. The RCMP has adopted the Integrity Regime administered by Public Services and Procurement Canada. As a result, the integrity provisions are being applied in RCMP contracting activities as outlined in this solicitation. Canada will make available Notices of Proposed Procurement (NPP), bid solicitations and related documents for download through the Government Electronic Tendering Service (GETS) at https://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities . Canada is not responsible and will not assume any liabilities whatsoever for the information found on websites of third parties. In the event an NPP, bid solicitation or related documentation would be amended, Canada will not be sending notifications. Canada will post all amendments, including significant enquiries received and their replies, using GETS. It is the sole responsibility of the Bidder to regularly consult GETS for the most up-to-date information. Canada will not be liable for any oversight on the Bidder's part nor for notification services offered by a third party. Indigenous Procurement: The federal Indigenous Business Directory (IBD) is an online resource for all levels of government and the private sector to identify Indigenous business capacity. Having a business profile in the IBD will increase your company’s visibility and may provide additional business. A profile in the IBD can also allow you to compete for federal government contracts that are set-aside for Indigenous businesses through the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Businesses. For more information and to review eligibility criteria and register, visit: www.canada.ca/indigenousbusinessdirectory.

description:
Zugerland Verkehrsbetriebe AG (ZVB) intends to redevelop its centrally located site in the village center of Oberägeri, which currently houses the old bus depot.

The Municipality of Oberägeri plans to build a care center on part of the site, while ZVB aims to develop family apartments on the remaining area.

This selective design study competition seeks a project that is compelling in terms of urban design, architecture, open-space planning, and economic viability; the selected project must meet user-specific requirements and serve as the basis for the formal development plan.

title: Hydrogen Generator for Gas Chromatography
description: The United States Embassy seeks qualified and authorized reseller of one (1) on demand laboratory hydrogen generator, plus installation, gas distribution, commissioning, training and warranty services, as described below: PEAK SCIENTIFIC INTURA H2 250 HYDROGEN GENERATOR (AUTO-FILL), WITH MANUFACTURER'S STANDARD WARRANTY QUANTITY: 1 Peak Scientific part number: 3305698-0-02 (auto-fill) Flow rate up to 250 cc/min; 99.99999% purity; output pressure up to 175 psi Standard warranty: 12-month comprehensive warranty and 36-month PEM cell warranty both starting at Government acceptance Operator's manual and warranty certificate in English PEAK INTURA H2 ANNUAL SERVICE KIT QUANTITY: 1 Peak Scientific part number: 3306178 ON-SITE INSTALLATION, GAS DISTRIBUTION, COMMISSIONING AND TRAINING QUANTITY: 1 Firm-fixed price. No extra labor-hour charges. Performed at IFSLM, Kingston, Jamaica, by Peak-certified technicians, in English. Supply and install all clean, GC-grade tubing, fittings, tees/manifolds and point-of-use regulators to deliver hydrogen to the Agilent 7890A GC/5975C VL MSD and the Agilent 7890A GC-FID, which sit next to each other. Connect the generator to the lab's existing DI water supply for auto-fill. Leak-test every connection. Show that each instrument works on generator-supplied hydrogen, including the switch from helium to hydrogen carrier gas on the 5975C system. Provide one (1) day of on-site operator training for approximately ten (10) IFSLM staff, covering operation, routine maintenance, water quality requirements and hydrogen safety, including safe hydrogen use in the GC oven and MSD. Provide an installation and commissioning report. 004 � SHIPPING TO KINGSTON, JAMAICA QUANTITY: 1 FOB Destination: U.S. Embassy Kingston, 142 Old Hope Road Kingston 6 Jamaica, including all customs, brokerage, insurance and freight charges for the items to be delivered door to door (DTP). Contractor bears risk of loss until Government acceptance at the embassy.

description: The fee-based service contract covers the provision of technical assistance and support services to the European Commission for the ensuring of the effective implementation, monitoring and management of cross-border and trans-national cooperation programmes and preparatory activities for the next MFF programming period. The contractor will deliver expertise in programme management, monitoring, evaluation, and stakeholder coordination. Services include analytical support, drafting reports and studies, organising workshops and events, and maintaining knowledge-sharing platforms. The contractor will also support project selection, assessment processes, and capacity-building activities for programme beneficiaries. All services must align with EU regulations and the strategic objectives of the programmes. The nature of the work is demand-driven, varying according to programme priorities and emerging needs. Quantities of services will be defined through specific assignments, including expert days, operational support, and deliverables. The overall aim is to ensure efficient, transparent, and high-quality programme implementation. The contract contributes to policy learning, knowledge exchange, and enhanced cooperation among participating regions. By providing flexible and specialised support, the contractor enables the programmes to meet their objectives. (2026CE160AT059)

description: The purpose of this Statement of Work (SOW) is to outline the scope, deliverables, and responsibilities for the relocation of gear, machinery, and storage equipment from two existing warehouses (Bldgs. 54938/54805; 15160 Scrub Jay St Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, FL 32920) into an adjacent facility (Hangar AO; 60530 Hangar Rd Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, FL 32920) that is approximately 1/4 mile away. This project requires careful inventory management, safe transport of delicate machinery, and precise placement to ensure minimal operational downtime for Detachment 3. Equipment to be moved includes, but is not limited to: sewing machines, cargo parachutes, personnel parachutes, boat motors, floatation rafts, Vidmar/toolboxes, supply cabinets, printers, storage lockers, and air drop-able rescue equipment packages that consist of jet skis and boats. The target move-in date is 2 November 2026. (Target move in date is an outdated figure. Please disregard this detail in the statement of work.) The government is instead requesting completion as soon as possible and no later than 30 days after award. See statement of work (SOW) attachment for full project description. Site Visit for this effort is mandatory as the governmnet will not be proving measurements of buildings and items to be transported. Contractors are responsible to take all nessecary measurements themselves. title: BD FACSMelody BRV
description: NOTICE OF INTENT � SOLE-SOURCE ACQUISITION The National Institutes of Health (NIH), National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases (NIAMS), intends to award a Firm-Fixed-Price Purchase Order to BD Biosciences for a Base + Two Option Years service agreement on the BD FACSMelody BRV 9-Color Plate 4way Cell Sorter. Description of the Requirement NIAMS requires a Base + Two Option Years service agreement providing remedial repair services and preventive maintenance for the BD FACSMelody BRV 9-Color Plate 4way Cell Sorter, Serial No. R6538850040, located in Building 50, Bethesda, MD. The agreement covers the sorter, its three lasers, and one computer workstation (printers excluded). The service agreement maintains the instrument�s performance and availability for NIAMS Intramural Research Program (IRP) research. The base period is 01/05/2027 � 01/04/2028. Option Year 1 is 01/05/2028 � 01/04/2029, and Option Year 2 is 01/05/2029 � 01/04/2030. The contractor shall perform one (1) preventive maintenance inspection during each twelve-month period, including one (1) preventive maintenance kit. The inspection will evaluate instrument performance and include cleaning, calibration, laser power checks, optical alignment, and part replacement as necessary to maintain the instrument substantially in accordance with its published technical specifications. Inspections must comply with Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) equipment manuals. The contractor shall provide unlimited telephone technical support and unlimited service visits at no additional cost to the Government. The contractor shall respond to a request for emergency onsite service within two (2) business days. The contractor shall provide preventive maintenance, service repairs, and technical support between 8:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time, Monday through Friday, excluding BD holidays. Work outside these hours must be approved by both parties in advance. The contractor shall provide OEM-certified parts for all preventive maintenance and service repairs, including the 405-45, 488-20, and 640-45 lasers, at no additional cost to the Government. Consumables are excluded. The contractor shall not charge the Government for shipping and handling of covered replacement parts. The contractor shall provide software updates released during the agreement term. The contractor shall use OEM-certified, factory-trained technicians for all preventive maintenance inspections, service repairs, and technical support. Justification for the Proposed Sole-Source Acquisition The Government intends to solicit from a single source pursuant to FAR 6.302-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. BD is the manufacturer of the FACSMelody and is the only source the Government has identified for the required service agreement. The service requires OEM-certified technicians, BD parts, and BD software updates. Preventive maintenance and timely repair reduce equipment downtime and support the reliability of research data for approximately 110 users. A service agreement with BD supports continued operation of the instrument and limits disruption to NIAMS IRP research activities. Response Information This notice is not a request for competitive quotations or proposals. However, interested parties that believe they can meet the Government's requirements may submit a capability statement demonstrating their ability to provide the required preventive maintenance and remedial repair services for the specified instrument and meet all applicable technical and operational requirements. The Government will review timely submissions to determine whether another responsible source is capable of satisfying the requirement and whether a competitive acquisition is appropriate. The Government anticipates making an award approximately five (5) calendar days after the closing date of this notice, unless the Government determines that another responsible source can satisfy the requirement. Capability statements must be submitted electronically to carly.beadle@nih.gov no later than 9:00 a.m. MST on November 13, 2026. Please reference Notice No. 75N98027Q00051 in the subject line of the submission. Primary Point of Contact Carly Beadle Email: carly.beadle@nih.gov

title: Electrical and Electronic Properties Measuring and Testing Instruments
description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE REQUIREMENT DESCRIPTION: The Naval Air Warfare Center Weapons Division (NAWCWD) intends to procure a commercial Radio Frequency (RF) record and playback solution. The acquisition consists of: One (1) Rohde & Schwarz (R&S) IQW Wideband I/Q Recorder One (1) R&S SMW200A Vector Signal Generator Associated software, licenses (including the FSW-B517 digital streaming interface upgrade), cables, and support. The required solution must be capable of playing back previously recorded RF signals from a Government-owned library stored in a proprietary R&S In-phase Quadrature (I/Q) format. The system must stream the high-speed I/Q data and convert it back to the analog RF data needed to stimulate the EA-18G aircraft's electronic warfare systems in a laboratory test environment. SOLE-SOURCE RATIONALE: The Government has determined that Rohde & Schwarz is the only source capable of satisfying this requirement. This determination is based on the following: 1. Proprietary Data Compatibility: The EA-18G program's critical test data library, which consists of terabytes of classified threat recordings, exists exclusively in a proprietary Rohde & Schwarz I/Q data format. The Government�s existing I/Q data library is maintained in proprietary R&S format. The required solution must use those files natively or otherwise demonstrate preservation of data integrity, metadata, timing, sample rate, bandwidth, phase coherence, and signal fidelity without introducing unacceptable schedule risk. Market research did not identify an available non-R&S solution that met those conditions. 2. Unacceptable Schedule Risk and Cost: As determined by market research (Sources Sought N6893627Q5001), The alternate OEM solutions evaluated by the technical activity relied on file translation, conversion, or non-native interface approaches that would require validation of converted I/Q data and present unacceptable data-fidelity and schedule risk. WesTest proposed an R&S-supported integration approach intended to avoid or control conversion; however, WesTest subsequently withdrew because it could not assure the required OEM-backed proprietary support. The Government�s existing I/Q data library requires native use of proprietary R&S-format files. Market research did not identify an available source, other than Rohde & Schwarz, that could furnish the complete required configuration including the proprietary equipment, upgrades, licenses, and OEM-backed technical support without data conversion or unacceptable technical and schedule risk. Response Instructions Responses are are due no later than 15 days After posting Submit responses by e-mail to: Primary Point of Contact: Stephanie Amoni, stephanie.j.amoni.civ@us.navy.mil, 564-230-3333 Secondary Point of Contact: Joyce Toye, joyce.n.toye2.civ@us.navy.mil, 858-978-4847 Use the following e-mail subject line: Response to Notice of Intent to Sole Source � N6893627Q5001� I/Q Test Equipment Capability Disclaimer: Information received will be used solely to determine whether to conduct a competitive procurement. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with preparation or submission of a response. Interested firms must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) database at https://sam.gov/.

title: Purina Dog Food RFI/Sources Sought
description: After reviewing this Request for Information, interested vendors are requested to submit responses by November 13, 2026, at 11:00 a.m. ET to the points of contact below. This is a Request for Information/Sources Sought Notice issued by the General Services Administration to gather information from prospective vendors interested in providing Purina dog food and related products in support of the National Stock Number Program and dog requirements. This is not a solicitation, request for quote, or request for proposal. The Government is conducting market research to determine vendor capability, interest, commercial practices, pricing structures, and recommended terms for a potential follow-on requirement. The Government is considering a firm-fixed-price five-year indefinite-delivery indefinite-quantity contract with one base year and four one-year option periods. Pricing for the base year and all option years would be submitted and evaluated at time of award. The Government is also considering a lowest price technically acceptable evaluation approach with price and technical factors. The specific acquisition strategy, evaluation factors, and terms and conditions will be identified in any future solicitation. NAICS Code 311111, Dog and Cat Food Manufacturing, applies to this RFI. Vendors interested in this potential requirement are encouraged to ensure their System for Award Management registration is active and includes the applicable NAICS code. Vendors are encouraged to register or update their SAM.gov record at https://www.sam.gov at this time. The Government may use responses to this RFI to determine the appropriate acquisition strategy, including whether any small business or socioeconomic set aside may be appropriate. All interested firms are invited to submit a response. The draft product list includes 27 brand name Purina products identified by the military veterinarian to cover a range of military working dog dietary needs. The Government only intends to include products approved by the military veterinarian. Based on current ordering history, and assuming outside the continental United States requirements are removed from the follow on contract, the Government estimates annual continental United States (CONUS) demand of approximately 5,500 bags of dog food. This estimate is based on ordering activity from extrapolating the most recent six months and may be refined as additional customer input is received. The Government is still assessing potential additional military demand, which is not included in this estimate. The Government anticipates that orders would be issued for direct delivery to ordering agencies. The Government is also considering requiring vendors to provide tracking and order status updates through a Government vendor portal. The information provided in this notice is subject to change and is not binding on the Government. The Government will not reimburse vendors for any costs associated with preparing or submitting a response to this notice. Requested Vendor Feedback Interested vendors are requested to provide brief responses to the following: Are you interested in this potential requirement, and can you provide all products on the attached Purina Food Plan list? If not, please identify which listed products you can and cannot provide. Some of these products require veterinary authorization/prescriptions. Can you fulfill orders for veterinary diet products that require authorization? Are any listed products unavailable, difficult to obtain, or subject to supply issues? What pricing structure would help keep prices low and competitive for this requirement? For example, tiered pricing, minimum order amounts, or another commercial pricing structure. Are you capable of providing MIL-STD-129R labeling, if required? If so, would this requirement affect pricing, lead time, or your interest in the requirement? What delivery timeframe would be commercially reasonable for CONUS orders? If awarded, would your company be willing to request access to the Government vendor portal and provide tracking and order status updates through that system? Response Information Please include the following in your response: Company name; Point of contact; Email and phone number; Unique Entity ID, if available; SAM.gov registration status; Business size and socioeconomic status, if applicable; Whether your company is an authorized distributor, reseller, or supplier of Purina products; and Brief responses to the questions above. Responses are requested by November 13, 2026, at 11:00 a.m. ET to Stephanie Bridgewater at stephanie.bridgewater@gsa.gov and Tracy Harper at tracy.harper@gsa.gov. Attachment 1: Purina Food Plan

Each inspection will evaluate instrument performance and provide calibrations, alignments, lubrication, and part replacement as necessary to maintain the instrument operation substantially in accordance with the published technical specifications for the instrument. Inspections must comply with Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) equipment manuals. Contractor shall provide unlimited technical support (telephone) and service repairs at no additional cost to the Government. If technical support is unsuccessful, contractor shall provide a service technician on-site within 48 hours. Contractor shall provide preventive maintenance, service repairs, and technical support between the hours of 8:00 AM and 5:00 PM, Bethesda, MD local prevailing time, Monday through Friday. Emergency service repairs and technical support must be provided as needed, based on MD local prevailing time, Monday through Friday, excluding BD Biosciences holidays. Contractor shall provide OEM-certified parts for all preventive maintenance and service repairs, except for consumables and lasers, at no additional cost to the Government. Shipping and handling for parts under warranty or contract shall not be charged to the Government. Contractor shall provide an OEM service technician to perform all preventive maintenance inspections, service repairs, and technical support. Justification for the Proposed Sole-Source Acquisition The Government intends to solicit from a single source pursuant to FAR 6.302-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. BD Biosciences is the manufacturer of the FACSymphony A5 Flow Cytometer and is considered the sole source for the required service agreement. Maintaining the instrument through appropriate preventive maintenance and timely remedial repairs is essential to preserving its performance, minimizing equipment downtime, and ensuring the reliability and integrity of research data supporting approximately 75 users. A service agreement with BD Biosciences is intended to support the continued operation of the instrument and minimize disruptions to NIAMS Intramural Research Program (IRP) research activities. Response Information This notice is not a request for competitive quotations or proposals. However, interested parties that believe they can meet the Government's requirements may submit a capability statement demonstrating their ability to provide the required preventive maintenance and remedial repair services for the specified instrument and meet all applicable technical and operational requirements. The Government will review timely submissions to determine whether another responsible source is capable of satisfying the requirement and whether a competitive acquisition is appropriate. The Government anticipates making an award approximately five (5) calendar days after the closing date of this notice, unless the Government determines that another responsible source can satisfy the requirement. Capability statements must be submitted electronically to carly.beadle@nih.gov no later than 9:00 a.m. MST on November 13, 2026. Please reference Notice No. 75N98027Q00036 in the subject line of the submission. Primary Point of Contact Carly Beadle Email: carly.beadle@nih.gov

title: MN USPFO CRTC Annual Scrap Metal Recycling
description: The Minnesota Army National Guard (MNARNG) at Camp Ripley averages 237,090 pounds of scrap metal in a year over the last five years. Payment for the scrap metal will be based upon the agreed upon percentage of the market index price for the date of the scrap metal removal from Camp Ripley. The amount of the payment will reflect each container picked up during the month minus each roll-off container change-out fee. All roll-off containers that are removed from Camp Ripley in a given month shall be accounted for on a monthly transaction report that reflects the following information regarding each pickup at a minimum: Date of Pickup, Price per Gross Ton, Weight (Pounds) of Scrap Metal, Total Price to Pay per Container, and the Container Fee per container picked up. Material shall be removed from Camp Ripley within 5 calendar days of notice of the container being full. The contractor shall weigh the material (scaling is not available on Camp Ripley) after removal. A monthly report shall be generated and sent to the Government POC listed on page 1. The contractor shall submit payment (if any due) for all scrap metal picked up during the month within the first 15 days of the following month. Contractor shall supply containers: 1. Three roll-off type containers are to be brought to Camp Ripley for collection of scrap metals 2. Each roll-off container should be 20 cubic yards minimum and 30 cubic yards maximum. 3. Roll-off containers will be located at the following locations: Camp Ripley Solid Waste Transfer Station Camp Ripley Ammunition Supply Point United States Property and Fiscal Office Warehouse Financial Terms: 1. Payment is due to within the first 15 days of the subsequent month. 2. Contractor will submit a monthly roll-up of all containers picked up during the month. 3. Certified Check/Money Order shall be made payable to �US Treasury� and sent to the following address monthly: United States Property & Fiscal Office � Minnesota Attn: Ariel Gould 15000 Hwy 115, Camp Ripley Little Falls, MN 56345-4173 4. Acceptable forms of payment include certified check or money order only. Bids are due by 10:00 a.m. CST on Friday, 13 November 2026. Bids may be delivered in person, emailed, or mailed to United States Property & Fiscal Office, Attn: Ariel Gould, 15000 Hwy 115, Camp Ripley, Little Falls, MN 56345-4173. Seller reserves the right to refuse all bids. Telephonic bids will not be accepted. Any questions are to be directed to Ariel Gould at ariel.d.gould.civ@army.mil. Emailed bids are the preferred method and are to be sent to: ariel.d.gould.civ@army.mil.

title: C1DA--PROJECT 528A5-27-503 A/E Design Replace Flat Roofs Canandaigua VAMC
description: Sources Sought Notice THIS ANNOUNCEMENT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. THE GOVERNMENT WILL NOT PAY NOR REIMBURSE ANY COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH RESPONDING TO THIS REQUEST. THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. The Department of Veterans Affairs is seeking a qualified Architect-Engineering (AE) firm to provide Schematics, Design Development, Construction Documents, Technical Specifications, Construction Period Services, Site Visits, Cost Estimates, As-Built Documentation, and all other related information for Project 58A5-27-503 Project Design Replace Flat Roof at the Canandaigua VA Medical Center, 400 Fort Hill Avenue, Canandaigua, NY 14424. this project is to develop a conditions-report and design documents for replacing the existing flat roofs on buildings 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 36, 37, 118, and various connecting tunnels. The conditions report shall be prepared after a thorough investigation of the existing conditions with estimated costs and improvements. The following design will include all selected repairs and improvements from the conditions report that fit within VA construction budget. As part of the report and design effort, the existing conditions shall be tested and verified, including evaluation of the drainage, materiality, masonry, fall protection, equipment, ACM, insulation, and structural integrity. New work may include redesign / reconstruction of support structures, drainage, roof type change, and parapet wall restoration to ensure water intrusion and legacy issues are mitigated. In addition to repairs and modifications, all interior drainage piping shall be replaced minimum 10 from roof drain unless, otherwise discussed with VA for convenience or practical reasons or as needed due to conditions of ease or degradation. This requirement is being procured in accordance with the Brooks Act as implemented in FAR Subpart 36.6. Applicable NAICS code is 541330 and small business size standard of $25.5 Million. Magnitude of Construction is between $500,000 and $1,000,000. This is a 100% Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business Set Aside. The anticipated award date of the proposed A-E Contract is on or before December 30, 2026. Potential contractors must be registered in SAM (www.sam.gov ) and are visible/verified/certified as SDVOSB in Dynamic Small Business Search (https://dsbs.sba.gov/search/dsp_dsbs.cfm) at time of submission of their qualifications in order to be considered for an award. In order to assure compliance with VAAR clauses, 852.219-75 VA Notice of Limitations on Subcontracting Certificate of Compliance for Services and Construction (NOV 2022) and 852.219-73 VA Notice to Total Set-Aside for Verified Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (NOV 2022), all firms submitting a SF 330 for this notice are required to indicate what percentage of the cost of contract performance will be expended on the concerns employees and in which discipline(s) and percentage of cost of contract performance to be expended (and in what disciplines) by any other consultant/subcontractor or otherwise used small or large business entity(s). Any consultant/subcontractor or otherwise business entity(s) used must be identified by name, office location and size/type of business (i.e., SDVOSB, VOSB, 8(a), small, large, etc.). Failure to provide this information will deem the firm s SF 330 submittal as non-responsive and preclude further evaluation All A/E firms are advised that in accordance with VAAR 836.606-71 the total cost of the production and delivery of designs, plans, drawings and specifications shall not exceed six (6) percent of the estimate cost of construction. Other A-E fees are not included in the six (6) percent. Additionally, FAR Clause 52.236-22 (c) - Design Within Funding Limitation, will be applicable to this procurement action. Evaluation Criteria is of equal importance with an exception of criterion 1 and 7 which shall carry an additional weight multiplier of 1.5. Each criterion shall be rated out of a score of 1 to 10. Total possible score is 80. Specific evaluation criteria include: 1.Specialized experience and technical competence in the type of work required, including, roof replacements, structural repairs, drainage, temporary systems and investigative services. 2. Professional Qualifications necessary for performance of site surveys such as the one described within the SOW including qualified personnel and approach to this scope. 3. Capacity to accomplish the work in the required time. 4. Past Performance on contracts with Government agencies and private industry in terms of cost control, quality of work and compliance with performance schedules. 5. Specific experience and qualifications of personnel proposed for assignment to the project and their record of working together as a team. 6. Location in the general geographical area of the project and knowledge of the locality of the project; provided, that application of this criterion leaves an appropriate number of qualified firms, given the nature and size of the project. 7. Specific examples of survey documents as described in the scope of work and approach to preparation of the documents as requested by the VA. 8. Record of significant claims against the firm because of improper or incomplete architectural and engineering services. Experience with government designs and construction. Experience with historic buildings, preservation, and alterations. description: Gegenstand der Vergabe sind BIM-Planungsleistungen (Einfach BIM) für die Erneuerung der Verkehrsstationen Friedrichshafen Flughafen und Meckenbeuren an der Strecke 4500. Der Leistungsumfang umfasst insbesondere die Erneuerung der Bahnsteigbeläge, die Erneuerung der Bahnsteigkanten, die Erneuerung der Beleuchtungsanlagen sowie den Austausch der Ausstattungselemente. Am Haltepunkt Meckenbeuren ist zusätzlich die Erneuerung des Stufenbelags der Personenunterführung vorgesehen. Folgende Leistungsbilder sind Bestandteil der Vergabe: - Objektplanung Verkehrsanlagen gemäß HOAI - Fachplanung 50-Hz-Anlagen einschließlich Bahnsteigbeleuchtung - Objekt- und Tragwerksplanung Ingenieurbauwerke für die Erneuerung der Treppenanlagen bzw. Treppenbeläge - Baugrunduntersuchungen einschließlich Baugrundgutachten - Erstellung eines BIM-Grundlagenmodells auf Basis der bereitgestellten Vermessungsdaten Die Planung ist unter Berücksichtigung der bahnbetrieblichen Randbedingungen, der Anforderungen an die Barrierefreiheit sowie der gültigen Regelwerke der DB InfraGO AG durchzuführen.

title: BBV Sublot 4 - HSST1020 - SALTLEY VIADUCT GABION WALL
description: Opportunity Summary - Gabion Retaining Wall Works We are seeking experienced suppliers and subcontractors to provide the supply, delivery and installation of a gabion retaining wall system as part of a civil engineering project. Scope of Requirements The successful supplier shall be responsible for: Supply of gabion baskets, including all lacing wires, diaphragms, ties and associated components required for a complete installation. Supply and delivery of Class 6G gabion stone suitable for basket infill. Installation of gabion baskets complete with stone infill. Supply and installation of geotextile membrane to the retained face of the gabion wall. Supply and placement of Class 6N/6P technical backfill behind the gabion structure, compacted in accordance with project specifications. Provision of all temporary works, plant, lifting operations, access arrangements, labour, supervision and ancillary materials necessary to complete the works. Volumes and Frequency This requirement is anticipated to be a one-off package of works for a specific project. Suppliers should be capable of providing both material supply and installation services. Further details regarding quantities, wall dimensions and programme durations will be provided within the tender documentation. Technical Requirements and Standards Suppliers shall demonstrate experience in the design support (where applicable), supply and installation of gabion retaining structures. Materials and workmanship must comply with: Project specifications and drawings. Relevant National Highways and/or Specification for Highway Works (SHW) requirements where applicable. Class 6G stone requirements for gabion infill. Class 6N/6P requirements for structural backfill. Manufacturer's installation requirements for gabion baskets and geotextile materials. Industry best practice for earth retaining structures, compaction and drainage provisions. Suppliers should have demonstrable experience delivering similar retaining wall or earthworks packages within infrastructure, highways or civil engineering environments. Service Levels and Quality Expectations The successful supplier will be required to: Deliver works safely and in accordance with approved method statements and risk assessments. Maintain programme commitments and coordinate deliveries to minimise site disruption. Provide competent supervision and trained operatives. Ensure all materials are supplied with relevant certification and quality records. Complete installation to the required tolerances and quality standards. Comply with project health, safety, environmental and quality management procedures. Delivery Location(s) Materials and works will be required at the project site location. Site details and delivery arrangements will be provided within the tender documentation. Suppliers should be prepared to coordinate deliveries and installation activities within a live construction environment. Additional information: Suppliers should be aware of the scale of this project and should assess their internal capabilities to be able to carry out the intended scope of work, prior to completing this expression of interest (EOI).

title: Balfour Beatty - Roads North of the Thames - LTC - Bridge Bearings
description: The Lower Thames Crossing Roads North Programme is seeking expressions of interest from organisations with experience in the design support, manufacture, supply and installation of bridge bearings for major highway and infrastructure projects. The scope comprises the provision of specialist bridge bearing product and methodology support to our Design Partner during the development of the detailed design, followed by the manufacture, supply, delivery and installation of bridge bearings to 16 structures across the Lower Thames Crossing Roads North project. As part of our procurement planning, we are seeking to better understand market capability, capacity and preferred delivery models to help inform the final procurement strategy and packaging approach. Through this PQQ, we are looking to engage with experienced suppliers who can provide innovative, durable and cost-effective bridge bearing solutions whilst supporting collaborative design development and safe, efficient installation. What We're Looking For We would like to hear from organisations with experience in one or more of the following: Proven experience in the design support, manufacture and installation of bridge bearings for major highway and infrastructure projects. Experience of working collaboratively with design consultants and principal contractors during detailed design development. Appropriate quality management systems. Relevant health, safety and environmental accreditations. Capability to manufacture and deliver products to programme requirements. Resources and expertise to undertake installation activities safely and efficiently. Experience of working within National Highways or similar major infrastructure environments is desirable. We welcome responses from organisations of all sizes, including SMEs, either independently or as part of a consortium, joint venture or wider supply chain arrangement. How to Apply If you are interested in this opportunity, please complete the attached Bridge Bearings Package Eligibility Criteria Questionnaire and return it to the Supply Chain Team by 13.11.26 at: BBLTCProcurementandSupplyChain@balfourbeatty.com Please ensure all sections of the questionnaire are completed, as this will help us gain a full understanding of your organisation's capability, capacity and relevant experience. The qualification questions have been designed to assess your ability to meet Balfour Beatty and Lower Thames Crossing supply chain requirements and will help inform the final procurement strategy for these works. We are particularly interested in understanding your experience in providing technical support during design development, your manufacturing and installation capabilities, available capacity, and your preferred delivery model for supporting major infrastructure projects. Additional information: The Lower Thames Crossing (LTC) is a new road to better connect Essex and Kent through a tunnel beneath the River Thames. Our purpose is to drive a change in how we deliver - connecting people to jobs and businesses to opportunities, leaving a skills legacy for the local community and construction industry, all whilst restoring nature and drawing a new blueprint for low-carbon construction. Our ambition is to deliver the UK's greenest road, and to do the right thing for local communities and the environment. We can only achieve this with the support of our supply chain, and it is therefore critical that for any supplier to be successful in winning work on LTC, they must demonstrate commitments to supporting delivery of our ambitions: • Delivering the works through a 'zero emissions' solution, and not using diesel on site in any plant or machinery. • Supporting us to leave a skills legacy for the local community, by not only recruiting locally, but upskilling your workforce to enable meaningful progression into higher paid higher skilled work. • Helping to facilitate successful opportunities by providing early careers roles, as well as inspiring young people into construction through delivery of STEM engagement.

title: Blanket Purchase Agreement for Portable Latrine and Hand-Wash Station
description: The Mission and Installation Contracting Command�Fort Bliss intends to establish five Blanket Purchase Agreements (BPAs) with eligible small business concerns for portable latrine and hand-wash station services at Fort Bliss, Texas, and associated training areas and ranges in Texas and New Mexico. Services include the rental, delivery, placement, anchoring, scheduled servicing, cleaning, pumping, sanitization, restocking, relocation, repair, waste disposal, removal, and pickup of portable latrines and hand-wash stations in support of military training, field exercises, and other mission requirements. This acquisition is a total small business set-aside under NAICS 562991, Septic Tank and Related Services, with a $9 million size standard. The anticipated BPA ordering period is 23 November 2026 through 22 November 2031; however, the Government may establish a later commencement date and corresponding expiration date to maintain a five-year ordering period. The Government will compete individual BPA calls among BPA holders. The BPA does not guarantee a minimum quantity of services or minimum expenditure. Interested vendors shall submit quotations in accordance with the combined synopsis/solicitation and all attached documents.

title: Tobyhanna Gates & Turnstiles
description: SEE PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT FOR DETAILS PART 1 � GENERAL INFORMATION 1. General This is a non-personal service(s) contract under which the personnel rendering the service(s) are not subject, either by the contract's terms or by the manner of its administration, to the supervision and control usually prevailing in relationships between the Government and its employees. 1.1 Description of Services/Introduction This is a non-personal service(s) contract to provide Gates, Barriers, and Turnstiles Service and Maintenance. The Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and non-personal services necessary to perform service and maintenance on vehicle gates, barriers, and personnel turnstiles at Tobyhanna Army Depot as defined in this Performance Work Statement except for those items specified as government furnished property and services. 1.2 Background Tobyhanna Army Depot (TYAD) relies on a comprehensive physical security infrastructure to protect personnel, equipment, and mission-critical assets. The vehicle gates, barriers, and personnel turnstiles are essential components of this infrastructure. Consistent preventative maintenance, emergency repair, and targeted technical upgrades are required to ensure continuous operational readiness and compliance with DoD physical security standards. 1.3 Scope The Contractor shall provide non-personal service(s). The Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items necessary to perform services as described in this PWS and associated contract documents, except for those items specified in Part 3 Government Property and Services. The Contractor shall perform to the standards and acceptable quality levels identified in this PWS and associated contract documents. 1.4 Objectives Ensure all gates, barriers, and turnstiles are adequately maintained to prevent failures and extend equipment lifecycle. Return damaged or degraded devices to full service quickly through a 24/7 emergency response capability. Maintain reliable function when activated to secure Tobyhanna Army Depot perimeters. Complete initial technical baseline repairs and upgrades safely and efficiently.

title: MDC BROOKLYN - REMOVE AND REPLACE SHOWER PARTITIONS
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial construction for MDC Brooklyn located at 80 29th Street Brooklyn, NY, 11232, and is prepared in accordance with the format in subpart FAR Revision Subpart 12.202(b)(1), as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes as the only solicitation; quotes are being requested and a written solicitation is issued (see attached). You are required to provide all pages of the written attached solicitation with your complete quotation. The Federal Bureau of Prisons (BOP) anticipates issuance of solicitation 15BBR027Q00000003 for the award of a firm fixed-price construction contract titled REMOVE AND REPLACE SHOWER PARTITIONS at the Metropolitan Detention Center in Brooklyn, NY. MDC Brooklyn is a federal correctional facility located at 80 29th Street Brooklyn, NY 11232. The contractor is responsible to provide all equipment and labor to remove and replace all existing shower partitions (with attached changing rooms) and bathroom stall partitions on the 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th, and 6th floors of the East Building at MDC Brooklyn. Each floor contains a North and South side, and each side includes: 6-bathroom stalls 7- shower stalls with changing rooms Changing rooms shall be 39.5 inches deep and include a door All partitions shall be floor- and overhead braced. Materials and finishes shall include: Powder-coated steel partitions 58-inch doors and panels Chrome zamac hardware Silver Vein color for all doors and panels Contractor shall also remove and replace all affected existing restroom accessories including, but not limited to, handicap grab bars, toilet paper holders, sanitary napkin dispenser, towel bars, soap dispensers, etc. Contractor to provide industrial standard labor and materials warranties from date of substantial completion. See the Statement of Work (SOW) attachment. The performance period for the project will be 60 calendar days from issuance of the notice to proceed. The timeframe allotted will allow adequate time for security clearances to be obtained, materials to be ordered and delivered on site, the removal of the old equipment, the work to be completed, system testing to be completed, and demobilization from the work site. Pursuant to Federal Acquisition Regulation 36.204, the estimated magnitude of the project lies between $100,000 and $250,000. (NOTE: This range is one of 8 available ranges from FAR 36.204 and is not meant to imply that the project has necessarily been estimated/budgeted to the maximum of the selected range. It merely conveys that the estimate/budget lies somewhere within that range.) Hard copies of the solicitation will not be made available. The website provides download instructions. Any secure/locked documents (if applicable) uploaded with the solicitation will require an active FBO vendor registration for access. If you encounter problems accessing these documents, please contact the Federal Service Desk at 866-606-8220. All future information about this solicitation, including any amendments, will also be distributed solely through this website. Interested parties are responsible for continuously monitoring this website to ensure that they have the most recent information about this proposed contract action. The NAICS code for this requirement is 332913 with a corresponding small business size standard of $15 million. title: Navajo Area Learning Management System
description: Title: Navajo Area Learning Management System Agency: Indian Health Service Issue Date: Friday, November 6, 2026 Due Date: Friday, November 13, 2026, no later than 12:00pm EST POCs: Responses must be submitted via email to carlton.taylor@hhs.gov. Include �Navajo Area Learning Management System � Your Company Name� in the Subject of the email and complete/return the IEE Representation Form This Sources Sought Notice (SSN) is for market research and planning purposes only and shall not be construed as a solicitation or an obligation or commitment to issue a solicitation by the Indian Health Service (IHS). This SSN is seeking information from the specific types of entities listed below to assess their capabilities in fulfilling the requirements set forth in this SSN. The information from this SSN will be used to determine the appropriate set-aside, if any, in accordance with the applicable regulations listed. The Government encourages the identified to respond to this Notice and will be assessed of their capabilities in the following priority: Indian Small Business Economic Enterprises (ISBEE) Indian Economic Enterprises (IEE) in accordance with HHSAR 326.603-1 Responses to the information requested will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method, including whether any ISBEE/IEE set-aside is possible based on the Contracting Officer�s reasonable expectation of obtaining offers from two or more relevant concerns that will be competitive in terms of market price, product quality, and delivery capability. An organization that is not considered an ISBEE/IEE firm under the applicable NAICS code should NOT submit a response to this notice. The applicable primary NAICS code for this requirement is 611420 � COMPUTER TRAINING. This is a purchase for a Learning Management System that meets the Federal Government�s FedRAMP compliance, including technical support, maintenance, updates and possible upgrades. Generic capability statements are not sufficient and may not be considered when assessing entity capabilities. Background Indian Health Service is an Agency within the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS). The Indian Health Service (IHS) is the principal federal health care provider and health advocate for Indian people, and its goal is to raise their health status to the highest possible level. IHS provides a comprehensive health service delivery system for approximately 2.3 million American Indians and Alaska Natives (AI/AN) who belong to 573 federally recognized Tribes in 37 states. Navajo Area Indian Health Service (NAIHS) is one of twelve (12) Regional Administrative units of the Indian Health Service (IHS). The NAIHS delivers Health Services to a user population of over 244,000 American Indians in five (5) Federal Service Units on and near the Navajo Nation. The five (5) Federal Service Units (SUs) include Chinle, Crownpoint, Gallup, Kayenta, and Shiprock SUs. Navajo Area Indian Health Service Office is located in St. Michael�s Arizona. This sources sought notice is seeking qualified contractors, to provide a Learning Management System (LMS) Portal. The Learning Management System Portal will supplement the Department of Health and Human Services� (DHHS) current Learning Management System to provide focused e-learning to meet accreditation requirements (e.g., The Joint Commission (TJC), Centers for Medicare/Medicaid Services (CMS)). The LMS will be available for all staff under NAIHS, including the Navajo Area Office, and the five Federal service units, which include primary hospitals and remote healthcare centers under each service unit. For the current submission and subsequent years, NAIHS is requesting a compliant Learning Management System that meets FedRAMP requirements. This recurring requirement keeps the current service level and licensing active. A complete Statement of Work is attached with the full requirements outlined. Summary Purpose and Objectives The Contractor shall provide a Learning Management System that meets the Federal Government�s FedRAMP compliance. The Learning Management System shall meet 508 compliance and be SCORM compliant. The Learning Management System shall provide focused clinical training courses applicable to accreditation requirements to meet health care accreditation (a) The Joint Commission (TJC) accreditation, (b) The Centers for Medicare/Medicaid Services (CMS) accreditation (c) Other applicable accreditation bodies. The Learning Management System shall provide a learning catalog that includes the following: (a) Safety and Infection Control (b) Advance Cardiac Life Support (ACLS) (c) Advance Trauma Life Support (ATLS) (d) Pediatric Life Support (PALS) (e) S.T.A.B.L.E (f) Neonatal Resuscitation Program (N.R.P.) (g) Other mandatory training courses listed in the attached SOW. The Learning Management System shall include an Authoring tool with the software component, allowing administrators to upload training and curriculum into the LMS. The Learning Management System shall include SCORM program with video storage for interactive course development, allowing administrator to upload training and curriculum into the LMS. The Learning Management System shall include technical support and maintenance, including updates and upgrades. The Learning Management System shall provide for documenting and tracking employee attendance, course completion checklists, and generating other reports that help the program and its users. The end users estimate around 5,000 Navajo Area IHS employees; this includes at least 1,000 contractors, volunteers, and tribal employees who work in Navajo Area Healthcare facilities. Additional details in the attached SOW. Note, all respondents must be registered on the SAM located at http://www.sam.gov/ prior to any potential award. Please see attached Statement of Work for full requirements. Past Performance Please provide any past performance information to support demonstration of your capabilities in the relevant technical areas and magnitude of work. Other Information (Optional) You may include any other information that may be helpful in developing or finalizing the requirements of the potential acquisition.
