title: RFI Comprehensive Medical Review & Audit Support
description: This Request for Information (RFI) is issued in accordance with FAR Part 10 to conduct market research. The Government's purpose is planning only; this notice does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP)/Request for Quotation (RFQ) nor a promise to issue one in the future. The Government will not pay any costs for responding, and any submissions become Government property and will not be returned. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future procurement. The Government is not seeking proposals or quotes at this time. Scope of Interest / Functional Areas: The Government is assessing the market�s capability to provide comprehensive support under the following disciplines: a. Audits for Medicare Parts A, B, D, and Medicaid medical record review and consultative services b. Audits for Medicare Part C medical record review and consultative services c. Evaluations and Inspections medical record review and consultative services d. Expert consultant and witness services in support of the Office of Investigations and/or Office of Counsel to the Inspector General A draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) is provided for industry feedback; requirements may change prior to any future solicitation. Requested Information (do not submit proposals or quotes): Please provide high level, non price specific information addressing the elements below. Do not include proprietary pricing, line item estimates, or any proposal/quote content. Section 1: Corporate Capability & Experience a. PWS Alignment: Demonstrate your organization's core capability to fulfill the functional areas outlined in the draft PWS. b. Medical Review Experience: Outline your firm's high-level experience in conducting large-volume medical claims reviews for audits and evaluations and inspections; and support services for medical expert consultants and witnesses specifically across the following five domains (as referenced in the attached PWS): 1. Audit Medicare Parts A/B/D and Medicaid 2. Audit Medicare Part C 3. Evaluations and Inspections 4. Office of Investigations 5. Office of Counsel to the Inspector General c. Geographic Reach: Describe your prior experience managing and executing nationwide or multi-jurisdictional medical claim reviews. d. Capacity & Scalability: State your organization's maximum monthly claim review capacity, including your approach to scaling operations between normal workloads and surge conditions. e Teaming & Subcontracting: Identify potential subcontracting partners or specialized vendors you would anticipate utilizing, including an estimated percentage breakdown of work performed by the prime contractor versus subcontractors. Section 2: High-Level Technical Approach & Operations a. High-Level Technical Methodology: Describe your conceptual approach to fulfilling the core tasks in PWS. Please limit this narrative to no more than 5 pages total, organized by the 5 PWS sections. Focus on your overarching claims review methodology, general sampling plan frameworks, documentation standards, and typical project timelines rather than a granular, step-by-step solution. b. Quality & Accuracy Frameworks: Outline your corporate quality assurance processes, internal review protocols, and standard strategies used to reduce error rates and ensure consistency across large volumes. b. Staffing & Key Qualifications: Provide a conceptual staffing structure or organizational chart. Identify the typical roles, credentials (e.g., MD, RN, CPC), and qualifications of the key personnel required to successfully support a PWS of this nature. Please identify whether these staff will need to be hired or if they are current employees/contractors. Also, indicate staffing availability for physicians with specialties (i.e. hospice, vascular surgeon, nephrologist, physical medicine and rehabilitation or physiatrists). c. Risk & Mitigation: Identify the primary technical or operational challenges anticipated with a medical review scope of this size and outline your high-level mitigation strategies. Section 3: Past Performance & Market Pricing a. Relevant Past Performance: Provide up to three examples of similar Federal medical review contracts performed within the last five years. Also, provide up to three examples of similar Federal support services for medical expert consultants and witnesses within the last five years. b. Performance Outcomes: Summarize the high-level outcomes of those past contracts, focusing on standard metrics such as timeliness, accuracy rates (including rate at which findings were overturned during the appeals process), and a history of successful audit findings. c. Cost Drivers & Efficiencies: Provide a general overview of your commercial pricing structure and the primary cost drivers (e.g., specific labor categories, specialized technology/AI tools, administrative overhead). Highlight any built-in efficiencies or innovative workflows in your approach that typically yield cost savings for the government. Section 4: Industry Feedback & PWS Refinement a. Clarity & Feasibility Review: Identify any requirements, metrics, or tasks within the draft PWS that appear ambiguous, overly restrictive, or technologically infeasible based on current commercial market capabilities. b. Recommendations for Improvement: Suggest specific enhancements, industry standard metrics, or structural changes to the PWS that would improve the clarity, feasibility, and competitiveness of the final solicitation. Submission Instructions: Email responses by November 13, 2026, 12:00 PM Eastern Time to the Points of Contact below. Mark proprietary information clearly; the Government may use non proprietary information to refine its acquisition approach. Points of Contact: a. Contracting Officer: Shavonda Jamison � Shavonda_Jamison@ibc.doi.gov b. Contracting Specialist: Dorothy Royster � Dorothy_Royster@ibc.doi.gov Attachments: a. Draft PWS (for market research and feedback only; subject to change). Disclaimer: This RFI is for market research; it does not commit the Government to any acquisition. The Government will not reimburse costs for responding. Not responding does not preclude participation in any future solicitation. No proposals or quotes will be accepted in response to this notice.

title: Tobyhanna Gates & Turnstiles
description: SEE PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT FOR DETAILS PART 1 � GENERAL INFORMATION 1. General This is a non-personal service(s) contract under which the personnel rendering the service(s) are not subject, either by the contract's terms or by the manner of its administration, to the supervision and control usually prevailing in relationships between the Government and its employees. 1.1 Description of Services/Introduction This is a non-personal service(s) contract to provide Gates, Barriers, and Turnstiles Service and Maintenance. The Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and non-personal services necessary to perform service and maintenance on vehicle gates, barriers, and personnel turnstiles at Tobyhanna Army Depot as defined in this Performance Work Statement except for those items specified as government furnished property and services. 1.2 Background Tobyhanna Army Depot (TYAD) relies on a comprehensive physical security infrastructure to protect personnel, equipment, and mission-critical assets. The vehicle gates, barriers, and personnel turnstiles are essential components of this infrastructure. Consistent preventative maintenance, emergency repair, and targeted technical upgrades are required to ensure continuous operational readiness and compliance with DoD physical security standards. 1.3 Scope The Contractor shall provide non-personal service(s). The Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items necessary to perform services as described in this PWS and associated contract documents, except for those items specified in Part 3 Government Property and Services. The Contractor shall perform to the standards and acceptable quality levels identified in this PWS and associated contract documents. 1.4 Objectives Ensure all gates, barriers, and turnstiles are adequately maintained to prevent failures and extend equipment lifecycle. Return damaged or degraded devices to full service quickly through a 24/7 emergency response capability. Maintain reliable function when activated to secure Tobyhanna Army Depot perimeters. Complete initial technical baseline repairs and upgrades safely and efficiently.

title: MDC BROOKLYN - REMOVE AND REPLACE SHOWER PARTITIONS
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial construction for MDC Brooklyn located at 80 29th Street Brooklyn, NY, 11232, and is prepared in accordance with the format in subpart FAR Revision Subpart 12.202(b)(1), as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. The Federal Bureau of Prisons (BOP) anticipates issuance of solicitation 15BBR027Q00000003 for the award of a firm fixed-price construction contract titled REMOVE AND REPLACE SHOWER PARTITIONS at the Metropolitan Detention Center in Brooklyn, NY. MDC Brooklyn is a federal correctional facility located at 80 29th Street Brooklyn, NY 11232. The contractor is responsible to provide all equipment and labor to remove and replace all existing shower partitions (with attached changing rooms) and bathroom stall partitions on the 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th, and 6th floors of the East Building at MDC Brooklyn. Each floor contains a North and South side, and each side includes: 6-bathroom stalls 7- shower stalls with changing rooms Changing rooms shall be 39.5 inches deep and include a door All partitions shall be floor- and overhead braced. Materials and finishes shall include: Powder-coated steel partitions 58-inch doors and panels Chrome zamac hardware Silver Vein color for all doors and panels Contractor shall also remove and replace all affected existing restroom accessories including, but not limited to, handicap grab bars, toilet paper holders, sanitary napkin dispenser, towel bars, soap dispensers, etc. Contractor to provide industrial standard labor and materials warranties from date of substantial completion. title: Sources Sought - Vehicle Lease
description: SOURCES SOUGHT Vehicle Lease Requirement in Alexandria, Virginia 140th Wing, Buckley Space Force Base, Colorado This is a Sources Sought notice for market research and planning purposes only. This notice is not a solicitation for quotations, proposals, or bids, and it does not constitute a commitment by the Government to award a contract or reimburse respondents for any costs incurred in preparing a response. The 140th Wing is conducting market research to identify potential sources capable of providing a vehicle lease for approximately 25 vehicles to support mission requirements in Alexandra Virginia. The Government seeks information regarding the availability, capability, and qualifications of both small and large businesses that can provide the required leased vehicle(s), including applicable maintenance, repair, roadside assistance, replacement-vehicle support, delivery, and pickup services, as applicable. The Government anticipates that any resulting requirement may be issued on a firm-fixed-price basis; however, the Government will use responses to this notice to inform acquisition planning and determine the most appropriate procurement approach. Requested Information Interested vendors are requested to provide the following information: Company Information Company name Cage Code and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), if applicable Business size and socioeconomic status Point of contact name, title, telephone number, and email address Business address Vehicle Lease Capability Description of the vendor�s capability to provide the required vehicle lease. Available vehicle types, configurations, model years, mileage limitations, lease terms, and estimated availability. Confirmation of whether vehicles can be delivered to and retrieved from Andrews Air Force Base, Virginia. Description of included support services, such as routine maintenance, repairs, roadside assistance, replacement vehicles, registration, insurance requirements, and emergency support. Identification of any minimum lease period, delivery lead time, usage restrictions, or other terms that may affect the Government�s requirement. Existing Contract Vehicles and Pricing If the vendor has an existing Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA), Federal Supply Schedule contract, indefinite-delivery contract, or other pre-priced contract vehicle that could support this requirement, the vendor should identify the vehicle and provide the applicable contract number, ordering information, relevant pricing schedule, period of performance, and any ordering limitations. Vendors should also identify whether the Government may place an order directly against the existing BPA or other contract vehicle, subject to Government review and applicable ordering procedures. If no existing contract vehicle is available, vendors may provide estimated lease pricing and a description of proposed pricing assumptions. Questions or Areas Requiring Clarification Identify any requirement details that are unclear, incomplete, or may limit the vendor�s ability to provide an accurate capability statement or estimated pricing. Provide recommended alternatives or commercially available solutions, if applicable. Submission Instructions Responses should be limited to information relevant to the vehicle lease requirement and submitted by the date and method identified in any accompanying notice or correspondence. Responses will be used solely for market research, acquisition planning, and decision-making purposes. The Government does not intend to award a contract based solely on responses to this Sources Sought notice.

title: LLA Navigation Lock Switchgear
description: Title: LLA Navigation Lock Switchgear Replacement: The work is located at the Lower Granite Dam, Pomeroy, Washington. The solicitation will be issued as a Best Value Trade-Off (BVTO) Request for Proposal (RFP) and result in a single firm-fixed price construction contract. This procurement is a small business set aside. 100% Performance and payment bonds will be required for this project. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS code for this project is 238210 Electrical Contractors and Other Wiring Installation Contractors and the associated small business size standard is $19 million. Solicitation number W912EF27RA002 will be posted to the SAM.gov Contract Opportunities website on or about mid November 2026. The proposal due date will be contained in the solicitation and any solicitation amendments that may be issued. The solicitation will be made available for download on the SAM.gov Contract Opportunities website. Offerors are responsible for checking the referenced page for any updates to the Notice. The Government is not responsible for any loss of Internet connectivity or for an offeror's inability to access the documents posted at the referenced website. Proposals will be due approximately 30 days after the solicitation is posted. The exact proposal due date will be indicated in the solicitation. System for Award Management (SAM): Offerors must register in the SAM at https://sam.gov/content/home prior to receiving an award. NOTE: The response date that is required to post this notice is not in any way a due date for any submission. This is a pre-solicitation notice only. Scope: The scope of the work involves replacing existing medium and low voltage switchgear lineups and their associated feeder cables with modernized medium and low voltage switchgear and motor control center lineups at Lower Granite Dam Navigation Lock. The main features of work includes: Provide and install one (1) new medium voltage switch gear. Provide and install one (1) new low voltage switch gear. Provide and install two (2) new motor control center lineups. Provide modernized controls for existing electrical loads. Provide one (1) new 4,160/480-V 1,000 kVA transformer. Provide lighting load centers to replace existing panels. Provide new concrete housekeeping pads for new electrical equipment. Provide new cable trays and conduits where required by circuit reconfigurations and to bring fill ratios to levels that meet electrical codes. Provide an HMI screen to replace an existing annunciator panel. Demolish existing medium and low voltage switchgear, motor controls centers, and transformers. Demolish the existing 480VAC feeders routed from existing low voltage switchgear and motor control centers. Seal hatch and any expansion joints, or cracks, to prevent water intrusion in an existing electrical room. This work is anticipated to be performed in 2028 and 2029, with cutover power construction work being completed during the 2028 and 2029 navigation lock outages. Access to the navigation lock deck and electrical substation rooms will be available for workers and equipment. THE GOVERNMENT RESERVES THE RIGHT TO CANCEL THE SOLICITATION EITHER BEFORE OR AFTER THE CLOSING DATE. NO REIMBURSEMENT WILL BE MADE FOR ANY COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH PROVIDING INFORMATION IN RESPONSE TO THIS PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE OR ANY FOLLOW-UP INFORMATION REQUEST. All on-site work shall be performed in accordance with the Corps of Engineers Safety and Health Requirements Manual (EM 385-1-1). Establish and manage an effective on-site Safety and Health program in accordance with EM 385-1-1 that will require the development and submission of a comprehensive project specific Accident Prevention Plan for Government acceptance. In addition, develop and submit for Government acceptance Activity Hazard Analyses for each phase of work and a project specific Fall Protection Plan that comply with EM 385-1-1. A Site Safety and Health Officer (SSHO) employed by the prime contractor is required for each shift of the contractor's on-site operations. The SSHO shall possess a minimum of 5-years� experience in construction safety on similar projects, shall have completed the 30-Hour OSHA Construction Safety training within the last 5 years, and shall have completed at least 24 hours of safety training from accredited safety training sources each year for the past 5 years. Establish and manage an effective Contractor Quality Control (CQC) System that will require the development and submission of a comprehensive project specific CQC Plan for Government acceptance. A CQC System Manager employed by the prime contractor is required to be on-site for each shift of the Contractor's operations. The CQC System Manager must possess a minimum of 5 years relevant experience in a supervisory or management position such as Quality Control Manager, Quality Assurance Manager, or Construction Manager directly involved in the management of construction quality at the project site. In addition, the CQC System Manager shall have completed the course entitled �Construction Quality Management for Contractors� within the last 5 years. Use the Government-furnished Resident Management System (RMS) � Contractor Mode to record, maintain, and submit various information throughout the contract period. RMS is a Windows-based program capable of operating on a stand-alone personal computer or on a network. The Government will make the quality control system (QCS) software available to the Contractor at time of notice to proceed. The project involves the development and management of Contractor furnished submittals for items such as pre-construction plans, product data, test reports, and contract close-out documentation as required by the technical specifications of the contract. Miscellaneous work within the project includes the delivery of As-Built Drawings, O&M Manuals, Contractor- Prepared Shop Drawings, and spare parts to the customer. Solicitation Number W912EF27RA002 will be posted to the SAM.gov approximately on around mid to late November 2026. The solicitation is a Request for Proposal Important Note: The SAM.gov Contract Opportunities Response Date listed elsewhere in this synopsis is for SAM.gov archive purposes only. It does not necessarily reflect the actual proposal due date. There is no response date included in this notice. The proposal due date and time will be contained in the solicitation and any solicitation amendments that are issued. Anticipated Award date is early to mid-March 2027. A site visit will be offered approximately 2 weeks after the solicitation is made available to offerors. See solicitation for details about the site visit. ACCESS FOR FOREIGN NATIONALS: Security clearance for foreign nationals to attend a site visit requires approximately 4 weeks; therefore, clearance should be requested immediately. To request clearance, please submit the names of all foreign nationals proposed for site visit attendance, along with documentation to verify that he/she was legally admitted into the United States and has authority to work and/or go to school in the US. Such documentation may include a US passport, Certificate of US citizenship (INS Form N-560 or N-561), Certificate of Naturalization (INS Form N-550 or N-570), foreign passport with 1-551 stamp or attached INS Form 1-94 indicating employment authorization, Alien Registration Receipt Card with photograph (INS Form 1-151 or 1-551), Temporary Resident Card (INS Form 1-688}, Employment Authorization Card (INS Form l-688A}, Reentry Permit (INS Form 1-327}, Refugee Travel Document (INS Form 1-571}, Employment Authorization Document issued by the INS which contains a photograph (INS Form I-688B}. Send this information by email to leanne.r.walling@usace.army.mil and jani.c.long@usace.army.mil Foreign nationals must have received clearance prior to being granted access to the project site.

title: FY27 ANNUAL FIRE DETECTION, ANNUAL FIRE SUPPRESSION & SEMI ANNUAL ANSUL KITCHEN HOOD INSPECTIONS, USP ATWATER
description: The Federal Bureau of Prisons (FBOP), United States Penitentiary in Atwater, California intends to make a single award to a qualified responsible entity to perform (1) Annual Fire Detection System testing, (1) Annual Fire Sprinkler/Riser Testing, and (2) Semi-Annual ANSUL Kitchen Hood Fire System Maintenance. They are located at United States Penitentiary Atwater, 1 Federal Way, Atwater, CA 95301. It is the Contractor�s responsibility to obtain permitting, should it be required. Annual Fire Detection System Alarm & Pull Station Testing: Inspection and testing of approximately 15 Simplex fire alarm panels, 35 annunciators, 540 smoke heads, 240 pull stations, 45 heat detectors, 140 duct detectors, 60 flow switches, and 70 tamper switches in accordance with NFPA 72. Annual Fire Sprinkler and Riser Testing: Comprehensive testing of approximately 53 wet risers, 3 dry risers, and 2 electric fire pumps in accordance with NFPA 25. Semi-Annual ANSUL Kitchen Hood Maintenance: Semi-annual inspection and maintenance of approximately 9 kitchen hood fire suppression systems located across two (2) kitchens and one (1) chemical/battery storage locker at the USP and Federal Prison Camp, to include replacing fusible links and spray nozzles in accordance with NFPA 96 Institutional Security Requirements (USP Atwater) The performance of this contract takes place within a high-security federal penitentiary. The contractor must strictly adhere to all USP Atwater institutional security regulations: Background Clearances: All contract personnel must pass a comprehensive NCIC background check.. Tool Control: All tools, equipment, vehicles, and test weights brought onto the reservation will be subject to thorough inventory, search, and strict tool control procedures at the rear gate entrance. Any missing tools will result in an immediate facility lockdown. Contraband: Cell phones, personal electronics, cameras, weapons, and drugs are strictly prohibited. Contractors may not bring personal items inside the secure perimeter. Evaluation & Award Award will be made to the responsible offeror whose quote represents the Lowest Price with Past Performance considered. Submission Instructions Interested small businesses must submit their written quotes via email to John Ridgeway j3ridgeway@bop.gov no later than 11/13/2026 at 09:00 PST]. Quotes must include: Company Information: Name, address, SAM.gov Unique Entity ID (UEI), and point of contact. Pricing: A line-item, firm-fixed-price quote for the full scope of work. All questions regarding this solicitation must be submitted in writing to the email address above no later than 11/09/2026.
